title: Add restrained haptic feedback to shopping gestures
requested: Feedback when switching between edit and shopping mode is activated.
Feedback when deletion, checking or unchecking is activated.

recommendation.requested_actions: One brief cue at an accepted action: a light tick for check/uncheck, a slightly firmer click for deletion, and a short confirmation for a mode change. Deletion is a successful action, not an error/reject effect.
additional_candidates: Undo: a short confirmation after one action is restored.
Reorder pickup: a light drag-start cue when a long press actually picks up a row; this helps distinguish dragging from ordinary scrolling.
Mode-pull threshold: optionally one light arming tick. If used, distinguish it from completed mode change and prevent repeated buzzing near the threshold.
recommendation.avoid: No vibration for every scroll movement, animation frame, key press, slideshow change or Undo countdown tick. Leave keyboard feedback to the IME. Start with the requested actions plus Undo/pickup; assess threshold feedback on a phone.

technical_review: For Qt 6.12 Android, use a small Qt/JNI bridge to the native View haptic-feedback API on Android's UI thread. Android recommends this semantic API: it requires no VIBRATE permission and respects system feedback settings. The user's linked XrHapticFeedback controls XR controllers. Qt supports Android-based OpenXR headsets such as Meta Quest; that is not the phone's built-in vibrator. Reuse existing Qt Core/Android support and existing AndroidX compatibility facilities where useful; do not add an XR module or haptic framework.
constraints: Preserve current gesture thresholds, pullback, action timing, order and visual feedback. Emit once per actual user action, not on model reload/animation completion or failed/no-op mutation. Respect system settings; unsupported devices and desktop builds should behave normally without haptics. API 28 needs compatible fallbacks for newer semantic effects.
verification_plan: Test action-to-effect dispatch through real gestures, Undo and pickup, including rejection, cancellation, duplicate signals and reload/no-op paths. Verify Android UI-thread/API fallback behavior, settings and package permissions/dependencies. A physical phone is required to judge feel and intensity; emulator dispatch tests cannot certify tactile quality.
scope: Research and backlog only; no haptic implementation or new dependency selected. UI-036 remains the active fix.
